newsitem.title: FRANCE: BAe joins Lockheed US fighter bid at Paris airshow.
newsitem.headline: BAe joins Lockheed US fighter bid at Paris airshow.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc said Wednesday at the Paris air show that it would team up with Lockheed Martin Corp. to bid for a next-generation U.S. fighter plane.

The Joint Strike Fighter is the Pentagon's attempt to squeeze maximum value out of a shrinking budget by buying a common airframe for the U.S. Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, which all currently fly different aircraft. The British navy is also buying the futuristic fighter.

"With a requirement for over 3,000 aircraft, JSF is the most significant trans-Atlantic military programme of the 21st century" British Aerospace Chief Executive Richard Evans said in a statement released at the air show.

British Aerospace's decision ends intense speculation over whether it would join Lockheed or rival bidder Boeing Co. in developing two prototypes apiece by 2001, with a planned entry into service in 2008.

The Joint Strike Fighter is expected to generate at least $100 billion in revenues for the winner over the life of the programme, with one senior U.S. aerospace executive estimating the price tag at $35 million to $40 million price per plane, depending on the version.
While fighter jets screamed overhead at the air show, executives huddled to cut deals and horse-trade over orders, which are the lifeblood of this intensely competitive business.

In Europe, eyes were riveted on Lagardere group and telecommunications giant Alcatel Alsthom, the rival bidders in the privatisation of French defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, launched by the previous conservative government.
The state sell-off is widely seen as key move in a consolidation of French and European defence capacity, needed to confront U.S. competition from the likes of Lockheed Martin.

Other orders announced on Wednesday included Brazilian airline TAM's purchase of up to 10 of European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie's A330-200 widebody twin-engined jets in a deal valued at around $1 billion.
U.S. airline Continental Express also ordered 25 EMB-145 regional jets, worth around $350 million, from Brazilian aircraft maker Embraer.
